sources.entry: Peel - Free, open source uninstaller and cleaner that removes apps with every file they leave behind, shows you why each file belongs, and moves everything to the Trash, so you can put it back. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/TuguiDragos/Peel) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.name: Peel
summary.one_liner: Peel is a free, open source macOS uninstaller that removes apps along with the leftover files they leave behind, explains why each file belongs to the app, and moves everything to the Trash so it can be restored.
use_cases: Completely uninstall a Mac app along with its caches, settings and support files
Find and review files an app left behind before moving them to the Trash
Free disk space by locating large files, duplicates and developer build artifacts
Reset an app's settings without uninstalling it
Review background items, extensions and Homebrew maintenance on a Mac
Set up Terminal with a theme, zsh prompt, and Git or ssh settings
summary.what_it_does: Peel searches the places apps keep files and labels each match with the reason it was found, such as bundle identifier, signing team, or a Homebrew cask. Files it is confident belong only to the app are preselected, while files shared with other apps are shown but not selected. Removed items go to the Trash, and its History feature can put them back. It also has Space pages for orphaned files, duplicates, installers, and large files, a Developer page for tool caches, a System page for background items and Homebrew, and a Tweaks page with macOS settings changes that can be reverted. The Terminal page offers themes, a prompt, and zsh, Git, and ssh options, and a peel command-line tool is included.
notable: Shows the reason each leftover file matched and how sure it is
Moves removed items to the Trash with a History feature to restore them
Ships a peel command-line tool with dry-run mode and is installable via Homebrew cask
Signed with Developer ID and notarized by Apple; GPL v3 or later source on GitHub
caveats: Requires macOS Tahoe 26 or later; does not run on earlier macOS versions
Some actions cannot be undone via the Trash, such as Homebrew's own uninstall and cleanups, resetting app privacy permissions, and Force Quit
Emptying the Trash is manual, and after that removed items cannot be restored
